question: Each cereal box hides one of 6 toys, at random. On average, how many boxes does it take to collect all six?
answer: 14.7 boxes, and the last toy alone takes 6 on average: the final few always cost the most.
move: Completing a set costs most at the end, as new finds grow rare.
ask: Which collection or checklist am I near finishing, and what will the last item cost?
hint: Add the average wait for each new toy: 6/6, then 6/5, and so on.
steps: With k toys found, a new one turns up every 6 ÷ (6 − k) boxes on average.
14.7 boxes, and the last toy alone takes 6.
source: Ross, A First Course in Probability, 2019
reference: Sheldon Ross, A First Course in Probability, tenth edition, Pearson, 2019
